source: CARDI Farmer Notes -- Domnoeb Sbeng Kok Rice Variety Guide (harvest & storage section)
text:
Harvest rice when the grain is well-ripened: when more than half the grains on the panicle have turned a mature golden-yellow color, and a fully mature panicle shows a dark golden/straw-yellow color, with healthy grains showing a pale, waxy sheen.

Drying: rice can be sun-dried on tarps, mosquito netting fabric, canvas or rubber sheets, or a cement floor -- this does not affect seed quality or cause variety mixing. A grain layer thickness of 2-3 cm is suitable for drying. Grain thickness and sunlight intensity are the main factors determining drying time and grain quality: on a clear, bright sunny day, dry for just 1 day, turning the grain every half hour; on a partly bright day, dry for 2 days, turning every 1 hour; on an overcast day, dry for up to 3 days, turning every 2 hours.

Storage: seed for future planting should be stored in tightly-tied plastic bags, then placed inside a second outer sack (double-bagged), kept completely separate from rice intended for eating, in a dry location free from rats, chickens, and ducks. Clearly write the variety name and harvest date on the sack. Harvested rice grain for consumption should be stored well in a granary, protected from rats and poultry, and kept away from moisture and dampness.
